Job Description 
 
 The College of Arts & Sciences has an outstanding opportunity for an Application Developer to join their team. 

 About this Opportunity 
 Reporting to the Lead Software Engineer, the Application Developer is responsible for building, testing, and maintaining web applications that support academic, research, and administrative workflows across one of the University's largest and most diverse colleges.

 This role works across the full application stack, including backend APIs, relational databases, data integrations, and accessible user interfaces. The position contributes to a modern Python-based application environment using frameworks such as FastAPI and works alongside senior engineers, infrastructure staff, and stakeholders to deliver sustainable, secure, and reliable services.

 This is a team-based position that provides opportunities for cross-training and skill development across related functional areas. The role includes supporting other engineers as needed and serving as backup to ensure reliable and continuous service delivery.

 Key Responsibilities 
 Build, test, and maintain features across the full stack of the team's web applications using Python and modern frameworks such as FastAPI. (15%)
 Work with senior engineers and stakeholders to translate business and technical requirements into application features that follow the team's established architecture and standards. (10%)
 Implement backend services, APIs, and data integrations that support application workflows. (10%)
 Build accessible, responsive user interfaces that connect to the team's APIs. (10%)
 Maintain and enhance existing applications, including their integrations with University systems and external APIs. (10%)
 Write unit and integration tests, and contribute to CI/CD pipelines supporting automated testing, builds, and deployments. (10%)
 Diagnose and resolve application issues and defects, bringing complex problems that span application code, data, and system integrations to senior engineers. (10%)
 Apply secure coding practices and address application performance and reliability issues. (5%)
 Participate in code reviews to maintain code quality and shared standards. (5%)
 Produce and maintain technical documentation for applications, APIs, and development workflows. (5%)
 Stay current with evolving technologies, frameworks, and development practices relevant to CAS IT's application portfolio. (5%)
 Participate in cross-training and provide backup support to ensure continuity of services. (5%)
 
Required Qualifications 
 To be considered for this opportunity your application must demonstrate you meet both the minimum qualifications and additional qualifications listed below. Equivalent education and/or experience may substitute for minimum qualifications except when there are legal requirements, such as a license, certification, and/or registration.

 Minimum Qualifications 
 Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Software Engineering, Information Systems, or a related field. Equivalent experience can substitute for degree requirement.
 Three (3) or more years of professional experience in software development, including full stack or backend-focused roles.
 Applicants who do not meet these qualifications WILL NOT be forwarded to the Hiring Department. 
 
 Additional Qualifications 
 Experience building web applications and APIs.
 Proficiency in Python or demonstrated ability to adopt new languages and frameworks quickly.
 Experience consuming RESTful APIs and working with relational databases.
 Experience using Git for version control in team-based development workflows.
 Familiarity with automated testing and CI/CD workflows.
 Understanding of secure coding practices.
 Demonstrated ability to work both independently and in a collaborative team environment while meeting deadlines.
 Excellent written and oral communication skills, including the ability to work with clients and colleagues with varying levels of technical background.
 Strong organizational skills, attention to detail, and creative problem-solving ability.
 
 Preferred Qualifications 
 Experience with modern Python web frameworks such as FastAPI, Flask, or Django.
 Experience with a front-end framework such as Angular.
 Experience working with relational databases, particularly PostgreSQL or MySQL.
 Familiarity with containerization and deployment concepts such as Docker or Kubernetes.
 Experience working in higher education or similarly complex institutional environments.
 
 Working Conditions 
 Work is performed in an office environment using standard computing equipment.
 Occasional evening work is required to apply security updates.
 This position may need to respond to service-impacting issues and coordinate with other technical teams to maintain reliable service delivery.
 
 Application Requirement 
 This recruitment requires a cover letter. Applications that do not include a cover letter will not be forwarded to the hiring department.

 About the Team 
 CAS IT provides technical and organizational leadership for application development, infrastructure platforms, systems integration, and technology services across the College of Arts & Sciences. The Applications and Development team builds sustainable, secure, and scalable systems that support academic, research, and administrative functions.
 With CAS IT, you will build software with purpose, including applications that directly support teaching, research, and institutional operations, while working in a collaborative engineering environment focused on thoughtful architecture, operational reliability, and continuous improvement.

 About the UW  
 
 Working at the University of Washington provides a unique opportunity to change lives – on our campuses, in our state and around the world.  
 
 UW employees bring their boundless energy, creative problem-solving skills and dedication to building stronger minds and a healthier world. In return, they enjoy outstanding benefits, opportunities for professional growth and the chance to work in an environment known for its diversity, intellectual excitement, artistic pursuits and natural beauty. 
 
 Our Commitment  
 
 The University of Washington is committed to fostering an inclusive, respectful and welcoming community for all. As an equal opportunity employer, the University considers applicants for employment without regard to race, color, creed, religion, national origin, citizenship, sex, pregnancy, age, marital status, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, genetic information, disability, or veteran status consistent with UW Executive Order No. 81 .
 
 To request disability accommodation in the application process, contact the Disability Services Office at 206-543-6450 or dso@uw.edu . 
 
 Applicants considered for this position will be required to disclose if they are the subject of any substantiated findings or current investigations related to sexual misconduct at their current employment and past employment. Disclosure is required under Washington state law .
